'''Ibiyinka A. Fuwape'''{{Audio|Ibiyinka_A._Fuwape.wav|listen}} (born 18 December 1962) is a [[Nigerian]] academic, professor in [[physics]] and the 2nd substantive [[Chancellor (education)|Vice-Chancellor]] of the [[Michael and Cecilia Ibru University]],<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2021-03-24 |title=Ibru varsity gets NUC's approval for 13 new courses, holds joint matriculation |url=https://guardian.ng/news/ibru-varsity-gets-nucs-approval-for-13-new-courses-holds-joint-matriculation/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2023-06-24 |newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]]|language=en-US}}</ref> a private university in [[Nigeria]].

==Early life ==

Ibiyinka Fuwape was born in [[Lagos State]] on December 8, 1962 to the family of David Ademokun.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Office of the Vice Chancellor|url=https://vc.futa.edu.ng/|access-date=2021-01-15|website=vc.futa.edu.ng|archive-date=2020-10-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201001001544/http://vc.futa.edu.ng/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She started her education at Reagan Memorial Baptist Girls Primary School, [[Yaba, Lagos]].<ref name="mciu.edu.ng">{{cite web |url=http://www.mciu.edu.ng/prof-mrs-ibiyinka-fuwape |title=The Vice-Chancellor – MCIU |website=www.mciu.edu.ng |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413043053/http://www.mciu.edu.ng/prof-mrs-ibiyinka-fuwape/ |archive-date=2018-04-13}}</ref> She proceeded to [[Methodist Girls' High School (Lagos)|Methodist Girls' High School]], where she earned her Ordinary level certificate, later earning her Higher School Certificate from 1979 to 1981 at [[Queen's College, Lagos|Queen's College Yaba]].<ref name="mciu.edu.ng"/>  She graduated from the [[University of Ibadan]] with a Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) first class honors degree in Physics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.mciu.edu.ng/the-vice-chancellor/|title=The Vice-Chancellor – MCIU|date=28 May 2018|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-04-17|archive-date=2019-04-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417135855/https://www.mciu.edu.ng/the-vice-chancellor/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She earned her Master of Science (M.Sc.) in 1986,<ref name="mciu.edu.ng"/> and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree in theoretical physics.<ref name="mciu.edu.ng"/>

==Career==

Ibiyinka started as an assistant lecturer in 1989 at the [[Federal University of Technology Akure|Federal University of Technology, Akure]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-05-16 |title=DID YOU KNOW? Joseph Fuwape, wife are VCs of separate varsities |url=https://lifestyle.thecable.ng/did-you-know-joseph-fuwape-wife-are-vcs-of-separate-varsities/ |access-date=2023-06-24 |newspaper=[[TheCable]]|language=en-US}}</ref> and was promoted to Professor in October 2003.<ref name=":0" /> She served as Acting Head of Department<ref name="mciu.edu.ng" /> and Head of the Physics Department for nine years.<ref name=":0" /> She also served as Dean, School of Sciences from 2011 to 2015. She was a member of the University Senate from 2003 to 2017, and acted as Chairman of the Senate during the 2014/2015 academic session.<ref name="mciu.edu.ng" /> She won the award of Dean of the Year in 2012.<ref name="mciu.edu.ng" />

Ibiyinka Fuwape was a visiting scholar at Ohio University Athens, Ohio, United States of America (USA) from 2007-2009.  She has published several papers in reputable journals both locally and internationally.[https://www.thenewsnigeria.com.ng/2021/03/03/futa-professor-ibiyinka-fuwape-wins-african-union-scientific-excellence-award/]

She was an Associate Member of the Abdus Salam Center for Theoretical Physics in Trieste, Italy, from 1996 to 2002. Her research at the Center focused on non-linear systems.<ref>Women in Physics in Nigeria and Other sub-Saharan African Countries: Progress and Challenges https://absuploads.aps.org/presentation.cfm?pid=14321</ref> She became a Team Leader for the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics working group for women in physics in 2002 and is still actively involved in the activities of this group.<ref name=":1" />  In 2006 she became a Schlumberger Fellow, in a program established by the [https://www.slb.com/who-we-are/schlumberger-foundation Schlumberger Foundation] to support science and technology education.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=APS Meeting Presentation|url=https://absuploads.aps.org/presentation.cfm?pid=14321|access-date=2020-07-01|website=absuploads.aps.org}}</ref>

Her current research is about chaotic dynamics of the lower atmosphere.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ogunjo|first1=S. T.|last2=Dada|first2=J. B.|last3=Fuwape|first3=I. A.|title=Spatio-Temporal Variation of Nonlinearity in Tropospheric Zenith Wet Delay over West Africa|date=2020|url=https://www.dl.begellhouse.com/journals/0632a9d54950b268,6dfc7a175c0f70bb,6b4bd76f097b9cad.html|journal=Telecommunications and Radio Engineering|language=en|volume=79|issue=11|pages=1009–1016|doi=10.1615/TelecomRadEng.v79.i11.100|s2cid=226617170|issn=0040-2508|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 2018, Fuwape was the recipient of the American Physical Society's Marshak Lectureship. Her address at the meeting of the Society was on the topic 'Women in Physics in Nigeria and Other sub-Saharan African Countries: Progress and Challenges'.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/international/programs/marshak.cfm|title=Robert e. Marshak Lectureship|access-date=2020-05-16|archive-date=2023-11-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103175213/https://www.aps.org/programs/international/programs/marshak.cfm|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was the [[African Union Kwame Nkrumah Award for Scientific Excellence]] (Regional), 2020 edition.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://pmnewsnigeria.com/2021/03/03/futas-fuwape-wins-au-scientific-award/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=FUTA's Fuwape wins AU scientific award|date=3 March 2021|access-date=8 March 2023|newspaper=[[P.M. News]]}}</ref>

She was named a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2022 "for decades of leadership in the advancement of women in physics in Nigeria and Africa, along with major research contributions solving problems in climate change, agriculture, and finance at the interface of physics and society, thereby benefiting economic development in Africa".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2022|title=Fellows nominated in 2022|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2022-10-19}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She is married to [[Joseph Fuwape]], former vice Chancellor of federal University of technology Akure.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-05-23|title=FUTA Governing Council Appoints Fuwape as New Vice Chancellor|url=https://allschool.com.ng/futa-governing-council-appoints-fuwape-new-vice-chancellor/|access-date=2021-01-14|website=Allschool|language=en-ZA}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
